source_reading.locator_rule: Hosted translator groups retained:1–3,4–45,46–68,69–73,74–80,81–83. Specific individual Sanskrit verse numbers not invented.

findings.notes: Explicitly Ruru’s son and born in Hiraṇyākṣa family; does not assert Hiraṇyākṣa is immediate father. Unknown mother/spouse remain unstated.
Air-only meditation on Brahmā in heart for1000years; agitation affects gods, Asuras and worlds; Brahmā arrives on swan and offers wishes.
findings.gap_or_recommendation: The event compresses world-agitation and swan arrival; these do not alter the bounded chronology.

findings.locator: 7.28.4–45, Durgama request and Brahmā assent paragraph
findings.notes: Request comprises all Vedic mantras with gods/Brahmins in three worlds and strength to conquer gods. Brahmā assents. No death immunity, weapon exception or boon expiration is stated. Null restriction/duration are appropriate witness-scope unknowns.
Brahmins forget Vedas, then bathing/sandhyā/homa/śrāddha/sacrifice/japa cease. Lack of havis progressively weakens gods; Durgama invests Amarāvatī, gods flee to Sumeru caves.
findings.gap_or_recommendation: Prefer explicit wording “Brahmins forget Vedas; rites cease” rather than only “forget Vedic rites”, which compresses epistemic loss into consequence.

findings.notes: Hosted account explicitly relates lost Homa to absent rain; drought lasts100years and kills humans/livestock. Fasted Himalayan prayer follows catastrophe. No inference that100years is tapas duration.

Goddess creates innumerable eyes, appears four-handed with arrows/lotus/bow/plant foods. Many eyes are not narrated biological children; Śatākṣī is their naming response. Translator fourth-dimension gloss excluded properly.

findings.locator: 7.28.4–45 final tears/prayer paragraphs;46–68 opening food distribution
findings.notes: Nine nights are continuous rain from tears, filling rivers. Gods leave caves and with Brahmins request food and Vedas. Thereafter food from the hand and further juicy provisions for humans/grass for beasts are given until crops arise. Śākambharī designation follows nourishment; army encounter follows messengers’ report.
findings.gap_or_recommendation: Nine nights qualify tears/rain, not an exclusive duration for the food provision. Current record preserves that distinction; do not infer festival dates.

findings.notes: Initial opposing army is1000akṣauhiṇīs. The later100destroyed is an intermediate loss, not a rival total.

findings.locator: 7.28.46–68, luminous circle and first battle paragraphs
findings.notes: Luminous circle encloses gods/Brahmins, Goddess stays outside to fight. Arrow rain causes darkness; arrows’ collision kindles fire and restores illumination.

All14record names match displayed list: Kālikā, Tāriṇī, Ṣoḍaśī, Tripurā, Bhairabī, Kamalā, Bagalā, Mātaṅgī, Tripurā Sundarī, Kāmāksī, Tulajā Devī, Jambhinī, Mohinī, Ccinnamaṣtā. They come out of Goddess’s body; emanation, not biological kinship. Distinct Tripurā and Tripurā Sundarī entries retained as displayed. Sanskrit spelling collation not performed.

findings.locator: 7.28.46–68, enumeration followed by successive host paragraph
findings.notes: 10000armed Guhya Kālīs and others; successive32,64and innumerable armed Śaktis explicitly appear. No restriction to a familiar ten-form list.
Śaktis destroy100akṣauhiṇīs; instruments sound; Durgama first fights them. Within10days all the akṣauhiṇī troops are destroyed. Avoid recasting100as entire army or adding1000new troops.

On11thday Durgama wears red, celebrates, mounts chariot, overcomes Śaktis and reaches Goddess; duel lasts2praharas. Current omission of red garlands/sandal and festivity is descriptive, not a lost battle transition. Six-hour gloss is hosted translator gloss; record correctly preserves prahara unit.
Arrow allocation is4horses+1charioteer+2eyes+2arms+1flag+5heart=15. Current record preserves targets and five-heart detail. Goddess kills him; no surrender or weapon-immunity exception inferred.
Blood vomiting and bodily death precede luminous vital counterpart merging into Goddess’s body. Merger does not erase narrated killing; peace in three worlds follows.
Goddess hands Vedas to Brahmins, calls them excellent parts of her body and directs careful preservation after remembered calamity. Return is explicit, not inferred solely from Durgama death.
findings.gap_or_recommendation: Recipient Brahmins should be made explicit in event/edge notes if graph needs transfer recipients.

findings.locator: 7.28.4–45 Śatākṣī naming;74–80 Durgā/name-remembrance address;81–83 disappearance/hearing benefit
findings.notes: Durgā name is expressly connected to killing Durgama; Śatākṣī cause was stated before battle. Goddess enjoins worship/service and reading deeds; both Suras/Asuras should serve her alone; disappearance and daily-hearing wish/Devī-Loka benefit finish chapter.
findings.gap_or_recommendation: Current single event compresses final injunctions and daily-hearing/Devī-Loka benefit. It should cite origin evidence for explicit many-eyes name-cause, rather than imply that causal naming explanation is newly spoken in74–80.

findings.notes: Six-event spine retains all major causal transitions from boon to rites-loss/drought, maternal rain/food relief, army attack/defense/emanations, quantified reversals/death and Vedas return/disappearance.
